title: Removing an initial program step
statement: Let $a,b,f,B$ be natural numbers, let $mode$ be Boolean, let $o$ be an oracle assigning a Boolean value to each of five indices and each Boolean word, let $y$ be a Boolean word, and let $st$ be a state of fifteen natural-number registers, each at most $B$. For any program instruction $l$ and Boolean answer $r$, if there is a finite guarded run that halts with answer $r$ from the configuration obtained by taking one program step from instruction $l$ and register state $st$, then there is a finite guarded run that halts with answer $r$ starting directly from instruction $l$ and register state $st$.
hypotheses_covered: oracle on five indices and Boolean words
each register of $st$ is at most $B$
one-step successor configuration has a finite guarded run halting with answer $r$
replaced:
Let $a,b,f,B$ be natural numbers, let the mode be Boolean, let $o$ be an oracle on five
indices and binary words, let $y$ be a binary word, and let $st$ be a register state
whose fifteen coordinates are all at most $B$. If, starting from the configuration
obtained by taking one step of the specified register program from instruction $l$ and
state $st$, there is a finite guarded run that halts with answer $r$, then there is also
a finite guarded run that halts with answer $r$ starting directly from instruction $l$
and state $st$.
